It also details supply shortages on the Apple Watch, AirPods and iPhone 7 Plus, with Cook admitting Apple "under-called" 7 Plus demand and "clearly missed some sales because of that," and it notes gross margin narrowed to 38.5% from 40.1% amid new lawsuits against Qualcomm over patent-licensing fees.
AAPL_2017q1.why_moved: The article states shares rose more than 3% in after-hours trading, which is consistent with the positive ret_2day_pct (+5.74%), ret_3day_pct (+6.21%) and ret_5day_pct (+5.59%). Building on the detail above, the beat on both EPS ($3.38 versus $3.22 expected) and revenue (a record $78.4 billion, ending the three-quarter decline streak) is the article's explicit anchor for the reaction, reinforced by the strong 18% services growth and record iPhone shipments — even though the piece is careful to note the growth rate itself was modest by the standards of past iPhone launches and that China and supply constraints remained live concerns, factors that likely explain why the rally, while solid, was not as dramatic as some of Nvidia's beat-driven moves in this data set.

sources.title: Apple Breaks Losing Streak, as Sales of iPhone 7 Shine Tech giant’s top line rises, ending a string of three straight quarters of decline, though margins are pressured

AAPL_2017q2.summary_analysis: The article reports Apple extended its rebound with rising profit and revenue even as iPhone shipments slipped 1% year over year to 50.8 million, which it attributes to continued weakness in China and customers waiting for the anticipated 10th-anniversary phone; total revenue rose 4.6% to $52.90 billion and profit rose 4.9% to $11.03 billion, Apple's first quarterly earnings increase in more than a year. Both figures beat expectations: EPS of $2.10 topped the $2.02 analysts surveyed by Thomson Reuters had projected, on revenue of $52.97 billion also ahead of consensus. Cook is quoted directly acknowledging the demand softness: "We're seeing what we believe to be a pause in purchases on iPhone, which we believe are due to the earlier and much more frequent reports about future iPhones." The article details a major capital-return announcement — a 10.5% dividend increase and a $35 billion expansion of the buyback program to $210 billion, part of a new commitment to return $300 billion to shareholders through March 2019, up from a prior $250 billion pledge — alongside cash reserves that swelled to $256.8 billion, described as exceeding the market value of 26 of the 30 Dow Jones Industrial Average companies. It also covers competitive pressure from Huawei, Oppo and Samsung's newly released Galaxy S8, a fifth consecutive quarterly China sales decline (down 14% to $10.73 billion), a bright spot in Mac revenue (+14% to $5.84 billion on the new MacBook), and a 13th straight quarterly iPad shipment decline despite a $28.7 million national ad campaign.
AAPL_2017q2.why_moved: The article states shares fell 1.9% in after-hours trading despite the EPS and revenue beats detailed above, and it identifies the specific driver: Cook's own disclosure of an iPhone purchase "pause" tied to anticipation of the next iPhone, combined with the 1% year-over-year shipment decline and a fifth straight quarterly China sales drop. That negative after-hours reaction is broadly consistent with the muted ret_2day_pct (+0.56%), though the figure turns modestly positive rather than negative, and the stronger ret_3day_pct (+2.41%) and ret_5day_pct (+3.22%) suggest the initial negative reaction to the "pause" comment was more than offset in the following sessions — a recovery the article, published on the earnings date, does not itself address, likely reflecting the record capital-return announcement it also reports gaining more traction with investors over time.

sources.title: Apple Continues Its Comeback Campaign, but iPhone Worries Persist Revenue has now risen in two consecutive quarters following a slump

AAPL_2017q3.summary_analysis: The article reports Apple delivered strong revenue in its typically weakest quarter, with total revenue up 7.2% year over year — its best growth rate in seven quarters — as iPhone shipments rose 1.6% to 41.03 million, Mac sales rose 6.7% for a third consecutive quarterly gain, and iPad shipments grew for the first time in 14 quarters, up 15% to 11.42 million units on strong sales to schools and businesses. Profit rose 12% to $8.72 billion, a second consecutive quarterly earnings increase after a yearlong downturn, and EPS of $1.67 beat the $1.57 analysts surveyed by Thomson Reuters had expected on revenue of $44.9 billion. Cook is quoted saying "we've got some momentum" and that "a lot of things we've been working on a long time are beginning to show in the results," while also acknowledging "we believe there is a pause" in iPhone purchases ahead of the fall launch, which he said "probably bodes well for the future." Guidance for the current quarter of $49 billion to $52 billion "mostly eclipsed" the $49.2 billion analyst consensus, a signal analyst Brian White of Drexel Hamilton said suggested Apple was not running into production problems with its upcoming iPhones. Greater China sales fell 9.5% to $8 billion, the first time in five quarters the decline wasn't in double digits, with Cook citing flat mainland China sales and 20% growth in Taiwan; the article also notes gross margin of 38.5% beat the 38.2% analysts expected even as industrywide memory-price inflation pressured margins broadly, and it details a new $1 billion U.S. manufacturing investment fund amid pressure from the Trump administration.
AAPL_2017q3.why_moved: Notably, this article never states the stock's after-hours or next-day reaction anywhere in the text — unlike nearly every other Apple report in this set, there is no explicit percentage move mentioned, so the source text itself does not explain why the stock moved as it did. What it does establish, as detailed above, is a genuinely strong quarter on several fronts: EPS and revenue both beat consensus, gross margin beat expectations, and forward guidance mostly cleared the Street's estimate, which would be consistent in direction with the positive ret_2day_pct (+5.51%), ret_3day_pct (+5.05%) and ret_5day_pct (+4.57%), but that link is an inference from the reported fundamentals rather than something the article itself asserts, and it should be treated as such rather than as a stated causal explanation from the source.

sources.title: Apple Sales Rise, Pushed by Purchases of iPads and Macs Sales of iPhones remain steady as consumers anticipate a new phone later this year

AAPL_2017q4.summary_analysis: The article reports Apple's best quarterly growth in two years, with a fourth consecutive quarterly revenue increase and third consecutive profit increase (profit up 19% to $10.71 billion), iPhone shipments up 2.6% to 46.7 million, and China sales rising for the first time since early 2016. Fiscal fourth-quarter EPS of $2.07 beat the $1.87 analysts had expected, on revenue up 12% to $52.58 billion, though annual revenue of $229.23 billion, up 6% for the year, remained below its fiscal 2015 peak. Guidance for the holiday quarter of $84 billion to $87 billion was well above the prior record of $78.35 billion set the year before. The piece devotes substantial space to iPhone X launch risk: the iPhone 8 and 8 Plus, which began shipping September 22, had "the weakest initial sales of any new iPhone in years" according to market-research estimates, and the iPhone X — shipping the day after this report, delayed more than a month by production issues — faced slashed unit projections (Strategy Analytics cut its estimate to fewer than 30 million units from 60 million earlier in the year) and long shipping delays for early online orders. Cook, interviewed directly, called demand for the X "very strong" and said "the ramp... is going well" since otherwise "we wouldn't be able to guide" for record revenue, while acknowledging launching three iPhone models with a staggered schedule made forecasting "complex" and that Apple doesn't "profess to be able to do it perfectly." Greater China revenue rose 12% to $9.8 billion after six straight quarterly declines, even as Apple's China unit market share slipped to 8.5% from 10% amid low-cost local competition, and services revenue surged 34% to $8.5 billion.
AAPL_2017q4.why_moved: The article states shares rose about 3% in after-hours trading, consistent with the positive ret_2day_pct (+3.04%), ret_3day_pct (+1.65%) and ret_5day_pct (+2.99%). As detailed above, the article ties the reaction to the EPS beat ($2.07 versus $1.87 expected) and a forward guide of $84-87 billion that topped the prior holiday-quarter record, along with the China revenue rebound after six consecutive declines. The roughly 3% move is comparatively restrained given the scale of the beat, which is plausibly connected to the countervailing concerns the same article raises — weak initial iPhone 8 demand and the iPhone X's production delays and slashed unit forecasts — though the article does not explicitly state that these risks tempered the stock's reaction; it reports the positive after-hours move and the iPhone X uncertainties as separate facts rather than drawing that connection itself.

sources.title: iPhone Demand Charges Apple’s Results Revenue and profit increase by double digits amid sales rise in China, and the company said it expects record revenue in the current period

AAPL_2018q1.summary_analysis: The article reports Apple posted record quarterly revenue and profit even as the number of iPhones sold fell, driven by the $1,000 iPhone X lifting the average iPhone selling price by nearly 15%; total revenue rose 13% to an all-time high of $88.29 billion (in a quarter one week shorter than the year-earlier period) even as iPhone units fell 1% to 77.3 million, and profit rose 12% to a record $20.07 billion. The article's central tension is the current-quarter guide of $60 billion to $62 billion, which it describes as "well below" analysts' recent consensus of $66.54 billion — a consensus that had already been falling for weeks on concerns about iPhone X demand and uncertainty around the iPhone 8 and 8 Plus. CFO Luca Maestri said the iPhone X had been the best-selling iPhone since release, telling the Journal "we're really, really happy with the way it's going," but the piece cites Canalys estimating Apple shipped about 29 million iPhone X units in the December quarter, roughly 6 million fewer than the company's targeted production, and quotes a consumer, Stephen Fleming, who chose a cheaper iPhone 8 Plus over the X to save about $200, saying "there was nothing about the X that said: I have to have this thing." The article also covers services revenue rising 18% to $8.47 billion, regulatory pressure over youth-smartphone addiction and the "batterygate" throttling controversy, and a $38 billion one-time repatriation tax tied to the new U.S. tax law.
AAPL_2018q1.why_moved: The article states shares gained more than 3% in after-hours trading Thursday, describing this as a rebound after the stock had been falling over the prior two weeks — but this stated reaction directly contradicts the given ret_2day_pct of -2.02%, which is negative. This is a case where the article's own account of the immediate stock reaction does not match the actual multi-day return data provided, and that contradiction should be stated plainly rather than papered over: whatever caused the negative two-day, and to a lesser extent three-day (-1.77%), return is not something this article's stated after-hours figure explains, even though the underlying weaker-than-expected $60-62 billion guidance (versus the $66.54 billion consensus) and signs of softer-than-hoped iPhone X demand documented in the piece are plausible candidates for a subsequent reassessment by the market in the days following the report.

sources.title: Apple Posts Record Results Even With Fewer iPhones Sold Tech giant says smartphone revenue rose 13% but projects weaker-than-expected sales for current quarter

AAPL_2018q2.summary_analysis: The article's headline news is Apple's record $100 billion stock buyback plan, described as the largest ever announced by a U.S. company according to Birinyi Associates data, alongside a 16% dividend increase, bringing total capital returned to shareholders since 2012 to $275 billion, including $200 billion in buybacks. Underlying results were also strong: iPhone revenue rose 14% to $38 billion despite only 3% unit-shipment growth, powered by higher average prices from the $1,000 iPhone X; total revenue rose 16% to $61.14 billion and profit rose 25% to $13.82 billion, the highest ever for a March quarter. Services revenue accelerated to $9.19 billion, up nearly a third and faster than the prior quarter's pace, with paid subscriptions reaching 270 million, up 100 million in a year, and the article cites Apple's goal of $50 billion in annual services revenue by 2020 (from $30 billion the prior fiscal year) and a Morgan Stanley estimate that services could drive 60% of Apple's revenue growth over the next five years. Guidance for the current quarter of $51.5 billion to $53.5 billion was described as "on track with" the $51.9 billion analyst consensus — an in-line rather than beat-or-miss figure. Analyst Arif Karim of Ensemble Capital is quoted saying the high end of the smartphone market is "very mature" and that the era of huge iPhone shipment increases is "dead," while Greater China sales accelerated to 21% growth, reaching $13 billion, and analyst Daniel Morgan of Synovus Trust said Apple is "reinventing the growth story."
AAPL_2018q2.why_moved: The article states shares rose more than 3% in after-hours trading, and it explicitly frames this as a response to the unprecedented $100 billion buyback and dividend increase layered on top of the profit beat (a 25% increase to a March-quarter record) and the accelerating services growth detailed above. This aligns with the strongly positive ret_2day_pct (+7.18%), ret_1day_pct (+2.1%), ret_3day_pct (+9.9%) and ret_5day_pct (+13.32%); the fact that the multi-day returns kept climbing well beyond the initial after-hours pop suggests the market continued to re-rate the stock on the buyback and services narrative in the days that followed, though the article itself speaks only to the immediate reaction and does not describe that subsequent multi-day momentum.

sources.title: Apple Allays iPhone Worries, Adds $100 Billion to Buyback Plans Smartphone revenue rises 14% as pricier iPhone X offsets slowing growth in shipments

AAPL_2018q3.summary_analysis: The article reports Apple delivered its best-ever revenue for its typically weakest fiscal quarter, with iPhone demand holding up despite a contracting global smartphone market and app-store/services revenue reaching a record. iPhone revenue rose 20% to $29.91 billion even as unit shipments rose less than 1% to 41.3 million, reflecting an average selling price up roughly 20% to about $724, which the article attributes partly to the $999 iPhone X making up an estimated one-quarter of iPhones sold. Total revenue rose 17% for a seventh straight quarter of accelerating growth, to $53.27 billion, above Wall Street expectations and near the high end of Apple's own guidance, while profit rose 32% to $11.52 billion ($2.34 a share), also above analysts' consensus. Cook is quoted saying "we're expanding our reach into emerging markets and seeing strong double-digit growth in revenue," and CFO Luca Maestri noted demand had remained consistent for the iPhone X, 8 and 8 Plus even in a seasonally weak period. Services revenue hit a record $9.55 billion, up 31%, and the article notes Apple's market value was approaching $950 billion, putting it "on the cusp of becoming the first $1 trillion U.S. company." It also flags real risks: escalating U.S.-China trade tensions that could expose Apple's roughly one-fifth China revenue exposure to tariffs, criticism from Chinese state media (including Xinhua and CCTV) over iMessage spam and App Store gambling apps, and Huawei having overtaken Apple as the world's second-largest smartphone vendor by shipments, according to Strategy Analytics.
AAPL_2018q3.why_moved: The article states shares rose 3.7% to $197.33 in after-hours trading, consistent with the positive ret_2day_pct (+5.65%), ret_3day_pct (+5.64%) and ret_5day_pct (+8.11%). Building on the detail above, the article ties the reaction to revenue and profit both beating expectations — profit up 32%, revenue near the high end of guidance — combined with resilient iPhone demand in a contracting global market and record 31% services growth, with the ASP-driven iPhone revenue growth on essentially flat unit shipments underscoring the pricing-power narrative the piece repeatedly emphasizes. The trade-war and Chinese-regulatory risks the article also details are presented as separate overhangs rather than something explicitly tied to tempering the immediate stock reaction.
